turns.t: Hello, doctor. I'm here for the hep C follow-up, I think? The letter wasn't very clear about it.
That's right. You finished your course of treatment in the spring, so today is about how you are and what we check next. How are you feeling in yourself?
Better, mostly. I mean, tired, I'd say. Still tired, if I'm honest.
How tired, and is it there all day or only at certain times?
Most afternoons I just hit a wall. Heavy, sort of, I can't explain it better than that.
Anything else you've noticed since you finished the treatment?
My joints are achy, knees and hands mostly.
When did that start?
Oh, I couldn't tell you. It crept up on me, I've no idea when it began.
Fair enough, that's very common. What about your tummy, any trouble there?
Now and then I feel queasy after fatty stuff, a fry-up or a takeaway.
Is your skin or the whites of your eyes looking yellow at all?
No, nothing like that. I'd have noticed, and so would the lads at work.
Good. Lie back for me and I'll have a feel of your tummy and look at your ankles. ~
Okay, go on. Sorry, cold hands! I mean you, not me. ~
Your tummy is soft with no tenderness, and your ankles look fine, no swelling.
Good. Is that good? ~
That's good, yes. Now, you've had a bit of a history with the hep C itself, which we're still confirming has cleared. Any operations in the past?
Just my appendix out when I was a teenager.
And do you smoke? What do you do for a living?
Never smoked in my life. I drive a delivery van, so it's a lot of sitting about.
That fits with the afternoon slump, partly. Tiredness after treatment is common, but I can't rule out an underactive thyroid yet.
Oh. Is that likely? ~

Not especially, which is why it's only on my list rather than a diagnosis. I'd like to arrange blood tests, including the viral load to confirm the virus has cleared, and a thyroid check at the same draw.
Fine. Do I need to fast? ~
No, you can eat normally. I'd also like to book an ultrasound of your liver, just to look at it properly after everything it's been through.
Right. And how long does all that take? ~
The bloods come back within a week, and the scan will be booked by letter. You can do the bloods downstairs after this. ~
Okay. Anything I can do about the tired afternoons? ~
Plan a short walk and a proper lunch break between deliveries, and try not to rely on sugary snacks to get you through.
That I can manage. What if it doesn't improve? ~
If the tiredness isn't any better in six weeks, come back and see me and we'll look again.
Right, will do. Thanks for explaining it all, the letter had me confused. ~
Any time. Take care of yourself, and drive carefully. ~
